heroText: Ålesund is a Norway base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Aksla viewpoint, add Art Nouveau Centre, and use Brosundet to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Ålesund International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: Origins
history.text: Legend has it that Gangerolf (outside of Norway better known as Rollo), the 10th-century founder of the dynasty of the dukes of Normandy, hailed from the island of Giske, north-west of the present-day town.
In 1793, the port of Aalesund was granted limited ladested rights.
On 1 January 1838, the new formannskapsdistrikt law went into effect, granting limited local self-government to all parishes in Norway.
In 1848, it was upgraded to the status of a kjøpstad, a more important market town.
In the night of 23 January 1904, the town was the scene of the Ålesund Fire, one of the most terrible of the many conflagrations to which Norwegian towns, once built largely of wood.

history.text: Practically the entire town was destroyed during the night, a gale aiding the flames, and the population had to leave the town in the middle of the night with only a few minutes' notice.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: After a period of planning, the town was rebuilt in stone, brick, and mortar in Jugendstil (Art Nouveau), the architectural style of the time.

history.label: Regional role
